structured_output.summary: The brief is strong on scope boundaries, local-only security stance and concrete pain-to-feature mapping. It is too broad for one pass, and it has a few gaps around localhost security, write-safety and contradictions with the team's own lane rules.

keep.title: Hard non-goals and local-only stance
keep.why: No accounts, no API key, 127.0.0.1 bind, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY stripped, zero deps. This removes whole categories of work and risk, and it is stated unambiguously.

keep.title: Diff-first writes with backups
keep.why: Every config edit shows a diff and is backed up. This is the app's core trust promise and it matches the 'safe file writes' bar.

keep.title: Pain-to-feature table
keep.why: Each pain from improvement.md (freezes, proposed ADRs, secrets in .mcp.json, model drift) maps to a concrete behavior, so features are testable and justified.

keep.title: Protected control-plane list
keep.why: Refusing to write hooks, settings, CLAUDE.md and scripts/, and never executing imported skills, keeps the app from becoming an attack path.

build.title: Backend core: safe-write engine + contracts/api.json
build.why: Atomic write, backup and diff, plus path allowlisting. Every other feature (Inspector, Plan, Health fixes) depends on it, and the contract lets the frontend and backend lanes proceed in parallel.

build.title: Team matrix + Inspector (models.json, consult.config.json, roster.json)
build.why: This is the highest-value pain removal: per-role tiers, drift detection and diff-first edits, with apply-models.mjs run after the write.

build.title: Health page (freeze.json, proposed ADRs, .mcp.json secret scan with redaction)
build.why: It is read-mostly, cheap, and covers three of the six listed pains. Build redaction first so secrets never reach logs or the UI.

build.title: Task-board composer with sequence numbers and supersedes
build.why: It fixes the 'builders missing messages' pain directly, and its file format is small and well defined.

issues.title: Localhost-only is not enough protection
issues.detail: A server that writes files and spawns the claude CLI can be reached by any web page the user visits (CSRF, DNS rebinding). The brief needs Host and Origin checks, a per-launch token or a strict same-origin policy, and no permissive CORS.

issues.title: Writing agent front matter conflicts with the team's model rule
issues.detail: The team rules say never hand-edit `model:` lines in agent files; only models.json plus apply-models.mjs is allowed. Must-have 3 lists agent front matter as a direct write. The brief should say model changes only go through models.json and the script, and it should say which front-matter fields are editable at all.

issues.title: Scope is too large with no phasing or acceptance criteria
issues.detail: There are 8 must-haves and 6 pains, with no order and no definition of done. Chat streaming, GitHub import, drag-drop and the plan builder are each a project. Rank them and add one testable acceptance line per item.

issues.title: Import and chat safety details are missing
issues.detail: The brief doesn't cover path traversal or oversized files when importing skills from GitHub or dropped folders. It also doesn't say how 'anything that writes asks first' is enforced in chat, or what 'pin to plan' stores from an advisor item. Both need a defined format.
